subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Where are tropical rainforests mainly located?
options: Around the equator, between the Tropics
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests grow in a band around the equator where it is hot and wet all year.

questions.q: Hot deserts are typically found at around which latitude?
options: 30 degrees north and south of the equator
questions.explain: Hot deserts lie near the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, around 30 degrees where dry sinking air dominates.

questions.q: Which biome is characterised by a layer of permanently frozen ground called permafrost?
questions.explain: The cold high-latitude tundra has permafrost, a layer of ground that stays frozen throughout the year.

questions.q: What best describes the climate of the tropical rainforest?
options: Hot and wet throughout the year
Cold and dry throughout the year
Warm with distinct wet and dry seasons
questions.explain: Rainforests have high temperatures around 26-28 degrees and heavy rainfall exceeding 2000mm every month.

questions.q: Tropical grassland (savanna) is mainly distinguished from rainforest by having:
questions.explain: Savanna lies between rainforest and desert and experiences a marked seasonal contrast between wet and dry periods.

questions.q: Which biome is dominated by evergreen coniferous trees found in a broad belt at high latitudes?
questions.explain: The taiga, or boreal coniferous forest, forms a wide belt across high northern latitudes below the tundra.

questions.q: In a food chain, organisms that make their own food using sunlight are called:
questions.explain: Producers such as green plants convert sunlight into chemical energy through photosynthesis and form the base of the food chain.

questions.q: Animals that feed directly on plants are known as primary consumers, or:
questions.explain: Primary consumers are herbivores because they eat plants, occupying the second trophic level.

questions.q: Roughly what proportion of energy is passed on from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explain: Around 90 per cent of energy is lost at each level through respiration, movement and heat, leaving about 10 per cent to pass on.

questions.q: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead plant and animal material are called:
questions.explain: Decomposers break down dead organic matter, releasing nutrients back into the soil.

questions.q: In the nutrient cycle (Gersmehl model), what are the three stores of nutrients?
questions.explain: Nutrients are held in three stores: living biomass, surface litter of dead matter, and the soil.

questions.q: In a tropical rainforest, which nutrient store is the largest?
questions.explain: In rainforests most nutrients are locked up in the dense living vegetation (biomass) because recycling is rapid and soils are thin.

questions.q: The removal of nutrients from the soil as water washes them downwards is called:
questions.explain: Heavy rainfall dissolves and carries nutrients down through the soil, a process known as leaching, which reduces soil fertility.

questions.q: In the food chain grass to grasshopper to frog to snake, the frog is a:
questions.explain: The frog eats the grasshopper (a primary consumer), making the frog a secondary consumer at the third trophic level.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major cause of tropical rainforest deforestation?
options: Clearing land for cattle ranching and agriculture
questions.explain: Commercial agriculture, especially cattle ranching and soya, is a leading driver of rainforest clearance.

questions.q: What is a common effect of deforestation on the soil?
questions.explain: Once trees are removed, roots no longer bind the soil and rainfall washes it away, increasing erosion.

questions.q: Why is selective logging considered a sustainable form of forest management?
options: Only certain mature trees are felled, allowing the forest to recover
The whole forest is cleared at once
It uses no machinery of any kind
It prevents any new trees from growing
questions.explain: Selective logging removes only chosen mature trees so the forest structure and ecosystem can regenerate.

questions.q: A country agrees to protect an area of rainforest and in return part of its national debt is cancelled. This strategy is called a:
questions.explain: In a debt-for-nature swap, foreign debt is reduced in exchange for a commitment to conserve an area of forest.

questions.q: A rainforest community sets up guided wildlife tours in a protected reserve, using the income to fund conservation. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Ecotourism generates income for local people while protecting the environment, making it a sustainable use of the forest.

questions.q: A farmer clears a patch of rainforest, but within a few years crop yields fall sharply. Which explanation fits best?
options: Most nutrients were held in the vegetation and rain then leached the thin soil
The soil was frozen as permafrost all year
There was too little rainfall for any crops to grow
The land became a hot desert overnight
questions.explain: Rainforest soils are naturally infertile because nutrients are stored in the biomass, so once trees are cleared heavy rain quickly leaches the remaining nutrients.
